acceptance.given: Package A requirements and proposed compilation, case-routing and regression contracts are available for inspection; their compliance and execution results have not been assumed.

oracle.expected: At compilation, only scripts/vdd/compile_plan.py publishes the current semantic plan and plan-ready, using self-hosted with development governance off. Compiler artifacts provide each behavior its own Acceptance, oracle, assertions, source references and failure intent, with explicit structural and scope checks. At controlled execution, only Quick Dev assigns present/missing/unverifiable from actual bound case observations; VDD publication alone assigns none. At regression and terminal closure, all present behaviors retain exact case/assertion coverage without production rewrites intended to manufacture RED. Derived evidence has authorizes=[] and does not grant implementation or acceptance authority. Any replay first rebuilds the original binding identity and then replays with that same identity. These are lifecycle and artifact checks attached to compatible foundation/migration coverage, not new validator features or independent production-write work.
forbidden: Semantic-plan or plan-ready publication by another owner, manual artifact edits, fabricated compiler state or historical-status substitution.
Development governance, current knowledge/Skill-input attestations, source-freeze, reviewer signatures, internal Bootstrap, authorization receipts or a new 95 report added for this repair.
Missing per-behavior Acceptance, oracle, assertions, source references or failure intent.
Present/missing/unverifiable assigned before controlled case execution or by VDD instead of Quick Dev.
Present behavior omitted from applicable regression or whole-plan terminal coverage, or reimplemented to manufacture RED.
Missing imports, absent tests, environment failures, timeouts or absent human approval treated as causal product RED.
A new controller, evidence writer, entry-materialization protocol or validator runtime feature introduced to satisfy this guard.
oracle.observable: During compilation/publication checks, inspect publisher provenance, selected profile, governance configuration and atomic obligation-to-contract coverage. During Quick Dev routing checks, reconcile each disposition with its controlled case execution and original binding identity. During Q6/Q8 closure, compare present-case bindings against applicable regression selections and the current whole-plan terminal case coverage, and inspect candidate changes for manufactured RED. A validator return value, filename or plan status alone cannot prove these boundaries.

acceptance.then: The inspected compilation, case-routing, regression and terminal artifacts satisfy the declared VDD/Quick Dev boundaries without adding product scope or implementation authority.
acceptance.when: The canonical compiler prepares and publishes the plan, Quick Dev performs controlled case execution and disposition assignment, and the compatible foundation/migration lane undergoes Q6 regression and Q8 terminal boundary evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: At canonical publication inspection, reject a current semantic plan or plan-ready claim without scripts/vdd/compile_plan.py publication provenance. This artifact guard is not a product runtime RED marker.
At compilation configuration inspection, reject development governance being enabled or governance receipts being introduced for this self-hosted repair.

At compiled-contract inspection, reject any behavior lacking its own Acceptance, oracle, assertion bindings, frozen source references or failure intent; do not replace boundary checks with runtime return-value assertions.

At Quick Dev disposition reconciliation, reject classifications made before controlled case execution, assigned by VDD, or unsupported by the actual case binding. Missing imports, absent selectors and environment failures cannot stand in for causal RED.

At Q6/Q8 coverage reconciliation, reject omission of present cases from applicable regression or terminal selection, manufactured RED through reimplementation, or replay without first rebuilding and retaining the original binding identity.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve existing VDD/Quick Dev lifecycle boundaries as compilation and terminal guards attached to the compatible foundation/migration context. This obligation authorizes no independent production change and does not reopen completed controllers.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: This governance guard changes no production, schema, persistence or controller behavior. Preserve historical failures and existing ADR-0041/ADR-0058 execution and replay authority; repair affected contracts through their canonical owner without rewriting prior evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Proposed compilation and execution contracts proceed through canonical publication, controlled Quick Dev observation and retained regression/terminal coverage; a boundary violation requires contract repair rather than product RED fabrication.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Canonical compiler publication and self-hosted/governance-off configuration are verified; every behavior has its independent complete contract; Quick Dev dispositions reconcile with controlled execution; present cases remain covered by a nonempty applicable Q6 regression selection and one current Q8 whole-plan terminal run. All four declared modules are selected only after their required tests are authored and behaviors exercised, with a 600-second terminal timeout. Earlier targeted commands use exact applicable current/predecessor node IDs with 300-second timeouts. Freeze tests/helpers/fixtures/selectors/plan/Acceptance before formal RED; invalidate affected proofs after shared dependency changes. No production owner is an immutable execution snapshot. If the first real validator call cannot legally be established, block before TDD rather than seed production, fake an import or fabricate receipts. Implementation workers neither self-accept nor commit/merge for the maintainer. No shared-controller, Phase, knowledge-publication, model-routing or historical-evidence changes are authorized.
